Root cause was TWO gaps, not one: (a) a ring arm dying on a non-quad left the cut partial, and (b) — the user's actual case — the vertical belt ring around the four frustum band quads CLOSES cleanly, a topological success that never touches the apex triangles or base sitting squarely in the cut's path. Restored the studio full-slice contract with two guards: ringParametricCutsSoup returns null when any arm stops on anything but ring closure or a true open border (raw edge-use counts distinguish borders from unwalkable neighbors), and meshLoopCutFacePreview discards a ring result failing the new lcRingCoversPlanes coverage check (every in-scope authored face the equivalent plane comb strictly crosses must have been subdivided) — both hand the cut to the plane comb end-to-end. Quad-everywhere shapes keep the parametric ring. Added the quad-walled-by-triangles refusal unit test and a 17th parity row replaying the exact user gesture (15 groups, apex split 4 apex-touching, editable consistent).
